NEW SECTION . 8.42 High-impact federal grants. 1 1. For purposes of this section: 2 a. “Federal guidance document” means a written statement, 3 memorandum, letter, bulletin, or advisory that is issued by the 4 federal government to a department or establishment and that 5 suggests or mandates a specific policy, procedure, or outcome 6 as a condition of receiving a high-impact federal grant. 7 b. “High-impact federal grant” means an award of financial 8 assistance by the federal government to a department or 9 establishment, including but not limited to a grant, loan, or 10 cooperative agreement, that does any of the following: 11 (1) Exceeds five million dollars in one state fiscal year. 12 (2) Requires a state matching expenditure of any amount. 13 (3) Requires the state to enact legislation. 14 2. A department or establishment shall not apply for or 15 accept a high-impact federal grant unless the department or 16 establishment has received prior approval from the general 17 assembly by law or from the legislative council if the general 18 assembly is not in session. 19 3. Prior to applying for or accepting a high-impact federal 20 grant, a department or establishment shall submit a federal 21 grant request report to the legislative services agency in a 22 manner determined by the legislative services agency. The 23 report must include all of the following: 24 a. The duration and dollar amount of the grant. 25 b. Any condition or requirement that is a condition of 26 receiving the grant. 27 c. A detailed analysis of any required state matching 28 moneys, including a maintenance of effort requirement. 29 d. A withdrawal plan describing how the department or 30 establishment will change the program or service funded by the 31 grant if the grant is reduced or eliminated. 32 4. The legislative services agency shall post federal grant 33 request reports on the general assembly’s internet site. 34 5. The legislative services agency shall maintain on the 8 general assembly’s internet site a publicly accessible database 9 of all federal guidance documents received from a department 10 or establishment. 11 EXPLANATION 12 The inclusion of this explanation does not constitute agreement with 13 the explanation’s substance by the members of the general assembly. 14 This bill prohibits a department or establishment from 15 applying for or accepting a high-impact federal grant, defined 16 in the bill, without approval from the general assembly or 17 from the legislative council if the general assembly is not 18 in session. For purposes of Code chapter 8, “department or 19 establishment” includes any executive department, commission, 20 board, institution, bureau, office, or other agency of state 21 government, excluding the courts and the general assembly. 22 Prior to applying for or accepting a high-impact federal 23 grant, a department or establishment must also submit a 24 federal grant request report to the legislative services agency 25 (LSA) that includes the duration and amount of the grant, the 26 conditions for receiving the grant, and a description for how 27 the department or establishment will change the program or 28 service being funded by the grant if the grant is reduced or 29 eliminated.
